Bill Introduced In Florida House Calls for Random "Drug" Testing of Welfare Applicants

TALLAHASSEE, Fla.

A "drug-testing" bill (HB 271) has been introduced in the Florida House of Representatives by Rep. Joe Arnall, R-Jacksonville Beach, which calls for random testing of people who apply for assistance under Florida's welfare-to-work act, known as Work and Gain Economic Self-Sufficiency (WAGES).

Opponents argue that people on welfare should no more face drug tests than corporate chief executives. House members also debated whether a requirement for health insurers to cover mental illness might be stretched to include alcohol abuse - even the ``town drunk'' - as they prepared several health care bills for final votes expected this week.
